name: Bellustar Tokyo, A Pan Pacific Hotel
positioning: High-altitude hotel in Kabukicho, Shinjuku, with guest rooms woven with Japanese culture, a top-floor spa and penthouses at 200 meters
best_for: Travelers who want sweeping Tokyo views from a Shinjuku base near the train stations
Guests looking for a design-led penthouse stay high above the city

facts.text: The hotel's address is 1-29-1 Kabukicho, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo.
The hotel is a 1 minute walk from Seibu Shinjuku Station.
The hotel is a 7-minute walk from Shinjuku Station.
Japanese culture is woven into the interiors of the guest rooms.
Spa treatments have a seasonal feel and incorporate natural ingredients from all over Japan.
The spa has treatment rooms and a relaxing lounge area.
The penthouses take their names from the Ten in Tenku and the elements of Kacho Fugetsu: Flowers, Birds, Wind and Moon.
Penthouse Sora is the largest of the penthouses and the hotel's flagship suite.
Penthouse Sora has east-facing windows that let in the morning sun.
In the maisonette-style Penthouse Tori, the bedrooms and living room are on different floors.
Restaurant Bellustar serves interpretations of French tradition using ingredients from various regions of Japan.
Bar Bellustar combines city views, innovative cocktails and immersive performances.

highlights.text: The penthouses sit at an altitude of 200 meters.
Guest rooms have windows seven meters wide offering a panorama of Tokyo.
The spa, SPA sunya, is on the hotel's highest floor and is named after the Sanskrit term sunya, meaning sky.
The penthouse floor is furnished with Karimoku Case furniture with design work by Keiji Ashizawa and Norm Architects.
The Sky Private Villa on the topmost floors features a restaurant three levels tall with views.

considerations.text: Guests arriving by car park in the Tokyu Kabukicho Tower car park.
Check-in assistance is given by staff on the 1st floor.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing reflects the luxury positioning.
